clue.text: Survive a heavy blow

parts.note: a fierce gale is a heavy blow in the weather sense, so coming through one is the literal and figurative picture

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hard punch and stays on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means coming through a crisis intact, pictured as riding out a gale.

clue.text: It's swinging in the rain

parts.note: evokes a dancer singing in a downpour, but means a blade sweeping to and fro across a car's glass

explanation.surface: A nod to a jaunty song-and-dance number in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade on a car's front glass swings back and forth whenever it rains.

clue.text: Worshipping a barbaric rain god

indicators.note: something barbaric is wild and uncivilised, so the letters of the words rain god are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Primitive people pay homage to a savage deity of rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring someone means venerating them, a synonym of worshipping.

clue.text: A fraction drunk

explanation.surface: A small part of something has been consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: One of two equal parts is a fraction; a half of beer is what gets drunk at the bar.

clue.text: Places visited on holidays, or between holidays

indicators.note: the word or is placed between letters of the holiday word, splitting it open

parts.note: rests are breaks or holidays from work
taken as written

explanation.surface: Destinations people go to on their breaks, or in the gaps between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts are towns or complexes that tourists visit on vacation.

clue.text: Bird dog

explanation.surface: A crisp two-word label for a hunting animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is both a bird of prey and a breed of hound used to hunt hares.

clue.text: Pole to feel sick on voyage

parts.note: S is short for the South Pole
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Someone from Poland gets seasick while travelling by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a Polish person but S, one of the compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sail is a trip on a boat, a synonym of a sea journey.

clue.text: Employment of paper folders

parts.note: suggests the work of office files, but means the pastime of people who fold sheets of paper into shapes

explanation.surface: A remark on the job of office document wallets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of shaping models by folding sheets is the occupation of paper folders.

clue.text: Attractive stretch revealed by guide

parts.note: magnetic means drawing things towards it
a compass is a range or extent

explanation.surface: An appealing stretch of country is shown to visitors by a tour guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational instrument showing north guides travellers.

clue.text: Soon led astray and may end in the soup

indicators.note: letters going astray wander off their course into a new order, here the words Soon led

explanation.surface: Something guided off course might end up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: pasta strips go into broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of pasta are commonly served in broth.

clue.text: Taking the offensive is a help in the boxing arena

indicators.note: the help word sits within the boxing word, placed inside it

parts.note: boxers fight in a ring
aid means help

explanation.surface: A boxer attacking gets assistance in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiding is launching attacks, going on the offensive.

clue.text: Bound to leave out

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to omit something.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip is both to leap lightly and to omit something.

clue.text: Retinue prepare for performance

explanation.surface: An entourage gets ready for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a procession of attendants; to train is to practise for an event.

clue.text: Break in, being unafraid of human contact

explanation.surface: A horse is broken in and loses its fear of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To tame an animal is to break it in; a tame animal is not shy of people.

clue.text: Profession for which many rush

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword shorthand for many
a rush is a marsh plant, a kind of reed

explanation.surface: A career that crowds of people hurry towards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profession' suggests a job, but here it is a profession of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of belief, as in a declaration of faith.

clue.text: Gun is taken to pieces in practice

indicators.note: a weapon stripped down comes apart, so the letters of Gun is are reassembled

explanation.surface: A rifle is stripped down during drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Employing something puts it into practical use.

clue.text: Looks at with an expression of friendliness

explanation.surface: Someone eyes another person with a friendly greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at; regards are good wishes sent to someone.

clue.text: Composer is brought back in irons, but set free

indicators.note: the reversed word is put inside the word irons
a prisoner set free is loosed from chains, so the combined letters are released into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word is is turned around, read backwards

explanation.surface: A recaptured prisoner is returned in chains, then released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns IS into SI, which goes 'in' IRONS; 'set free' then rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was an Italian opera composer, writer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Festival now beginning in the Orient

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the start of the word now supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A holiday is now starting in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern describes things located in or coming from Asia.

clue.text: A contest between two Poles and an Arab

indicators.note: the race phrase is placed between the two pole letters

parts.note: S and N stand for the South and North Poles
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A match between two Polish athletes and an Arab competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not Polish people but the compass points S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim.

clue.text: Gets information about raising money for the future

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
the information word goes round the word gets

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone finds out about fundraising for retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raising' reads the letters upward, so the built string is turned end to end; GEN is British slang for facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings put aside for later years are a nest egg.

clue.text: Mr. Kelly has a twitch-—it's hereditary

parts.note: Gene Kelly was the American dancer and actor
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A famous man has a nervous twitch that runs in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic traits are passed down through inheritance.

clue.text: Suit case put in the car

parts.note: gear is clothing, an outfit or suit
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A suitcase is loaded into the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit case' looks like luggage, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The transmission housing is a component fitted in a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Eccentric aunt upset about disease

annotationWithheld.why: Eccentric aunt upset about disease: TES (SET reversed) around TANU (anagram of AUNT) needs SET, but 'upset' would be both the word set and its reversal indicator, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Communication-possibly barbed

explanation.surface: A message that might carry a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is a telegram; barbed wire is a type of fencing.

clue.text: He is very selective about the movies he goes to

definitions.text: He is very selective about the movies he goes to

parts.words: He is very selective about the movies he goes to
parts.note: reads as a choosy cinemagoer, but means the statuette that is awarded only to a chosen few films

explanation.surface: A picky filmgoer who chooses carefully what to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is given only to selected films.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of the wine glass

explanation.surface: A loyal fan of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to staunch it; the stem is the slender part holding up a goblet's bowl.

clue.text: Embargo put on one in an Italian port

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a bar is a ban or embargo
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trade ban is imposed on a single Italian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a seaport on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: He plays a big part in children's tales

definitions.text: He plays a big part in children's tales

parts.words: He plays a big part in children's tales
parts.note: sounds like a leading actor, but big is literal: a giant monster in fairy stories

explanation.surface: An actor with a leading role in children's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant monster who eats people is a staple villain of fairy stories.

clue.text: You need your cases for this sort of holiday

definitions.text: You need your cases for this sort of holiday

parts.words: You need your cases for this sort of holiday
parts.note: suitcases are packed for any trip, but the phrase points to a pre-arranged all-in tour

explanation.surface: A reminder to pack suitcases for a trip away.
explanation.definitionFit: A package holiday is an all-inclusive tour, and luggage gets packed for it.

clue.text: Bloomer may be a big one

indicators.note: the letters of a big one may be arranged to form something else

explanation.surface: A blunder might turn out to be a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a flowering plant, so it blooms.

clue.text: Cash required to support athletes?

parts.note: reads literally as money for sportspeople who run, but means the everyday costs of operating something

explanation.surface: A question about funding for track stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Operating costs of a business or vehicle are its day-to-day outgoings.
